blocks.text: Article 368 sets out the general procedure for amending the Constitution. Different provisions may follow different requirements, so identify the type of majority and whether State ratification is required.

items: Some changes are made by a simple majority of Parliament and are not treated as amendments under Article 368.
Many constitutional amendments require a special majority in each House of Parliament.
Changes affecting specified federal provisions also require ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Do not treat every constitutional change as using the same voting rule. Learn examples of provisions in each category.
